66.t: Monk's rehearsal big band and the real beginning of bebop
66.s: Monk and Bud Powell rehearsed in a basement to create a new music for recognition; she says Dizzy created real bebop and Monk worked for Dizzy.
66.ch: Minton's, bop and the Monk circle
66.q: : He did start it, because everybody used to pitch in 50¢ or do arrangements and often I gave them money. They used to rehearse in the basement of some place, but the whole idea was, you know, like our black people never get credit, receive credit for anything they do or create. So what they were…

66.t: Bud Powell, Monk's big band and the house that built bop
66.s: Bud idolised Monk and played his compositions; the big band disbanded and everyone jammed at Minton's, 'the house that built bop'.
66.ch: Minton's, bop and the Monk circle
66.q: Yes, Monk and Bud Powell were together. I don't know how they were doing it, but Bud idolized Monk. He always did. Monk would write great compositions and Bud would actually play them very well.

66.t: Her apartment with the white carpet
66.s: Monk, Bud, Dameron, Dizzy, Miles, Sarah Vaughan and others came to her apartment to write and play; she has had the carpet since 1941.
66.ch: Minton's, bop and the Monk circle
66.q: Because most of them needed inspiration and they wrote the music up here at the house. I had a white carpet here on the floor. We used to sit on this carpet. I kept it clean, you know. We ate on it and did everything. Tadd Dameron and all the cats used to come. Monk used to come here and write his…

66.s: She saw Monk in New York in the 1930s and grew close at Minton's, where bop musicians jammed because 52nd Street had no work for them.
66.ch: Minton's, bop and the Monk circle
66.q: : I saw him in New York during the 30's. We became very, very good friends. In fact, Bud Powell, Monk, and I were inseparable. During the 40's that was every day, every night, all the time.

105.t: Meeting Max Roach and hearing Diz and Monk in New York
105.s: He first met Max Roach at the Capitol Theater in 1947 through Charlie Drayton, and at the Royal Roost heard Dizzy and Monk, with John Simmons describing Monk's playing between the cracks.
105.ch: Bebop, band changes and the road
105.q: At the Capitol Theater, and Charlie Drayton like I said, was the bass player. Well Charlie and Max were good friends. They were both from Brooklyn and they both played with Benny Carter. And Max came to the theater to see Charlie, came backstage, and Charlie introduced me to him. We met and the…

406.s: He does not remember Kermit Scott. He played clarinet in the Minton's house group with Nick Fenton, Monk and a drummer, and everybody sat in.
406.q: Yeah, with Nick Fenton and Thelonious and the drummer was Harold West sometimes and sometimes it was someone else. Just four pieces.

166.t: Back in New York, shaken, and hired by Monk at the Royal Roost
166.s: After two weeks indoors he went to work with Thelonious Monk in the winter of 1948; Monk's changed chord progressions kept jammers out.
166.ch: Los Angeles 1947-48, Rock Island and bebop in New York
166.q: Well, I stayed in the house for about two weeks, for fear that someone would say the wrong thing and it would bring out bad vibes with me, and then it would be physical combat, you know. So, when I finally decided to come out of the house, I got on the sidewalk, and it felt like an escalator. It…

0.t: Jam sessions at Minton's and the coming of bebop; Thelonious Monk
0.s: It was where Caldwell met Dizzy, Parker and Monk; he remembers Monk as a normal pianist who changed his style.
0.ch: The Jelly Roll Morton records and Minton's Playhouse
0.q: That's where it first started. That's where I met Dizzy, Charlie Parker, Thelonius Monk. We'd get off the bands and I'd say, go up there and play something, buy them drinks.

385.t: Minton's and the start of modern jazz
385.s: He says Minton's was where modern jazz started and that Christian was there constantly.
385.ch: Chords, recordings and his own groups
385.q: Minton's playhouse was the place... The place was Minton's -- Minton's Playhouse, that originally, the Modern jazz got started. The other places, they were open but they didn't accept it. There wasn't that type of musician down there in the first place. So if one or two of em came they would be out…

168.t: Minton's Playhouse sessions and keeping up with the new chords
168.s: He often went to Minton's where Monk, Clarke and Dizzy worked out bebop; Crouch describes cutting sessions, and Stewart says his ear saved him.
168.q: And -- oh, gee. Let's see. It's hard for me right now to exactly remember. But all those whom from time to time who we have mentioned passed through Minton's Playhouse. Those were some good, beautiful sessions.

169.t: Joining Coleman Hawkins; catching up on Minton's repertoire
169.s: Pettiford introduces him to Hawkins, who hires him; McGhee has to learn Monk's tunes and the bebop melodies at Minton's.
169.ch: Georgie Auld, Hawkins and Los Angeles
169.q: in... He was going with Hawk, and Hawk was going to California, and I heard about it, so he asked me was I interested, and I told him "Damn right." I wanted to get to California, because December here in New York wasn't too cool! I said, "Yeah, I'd love to be out in California." So anyway, he…
